title: laplace.packet-return/2
description: The versioned packet return carrier for authored completion, incomplete work, blocking conditions and interruption. Version 1 remains available for historical receipts. Exact source/artifact pins and continuation name retained work; schema validity never certifies goal completion or authorizes replay.

schema_version.description: This schema's $id; the version check-return resolves the validating schema by.

packet.description: The packet label from the plan's agents list, verbatim.

role.description: Which turn of the packet this return is: the first build, a continuation after a rejection, or the wave's synthesis.

status.description: Goal standing, distinct from provider turn termination. COMPLETE alone certifies the declared work; fixable remaining work is not demonstrated impossibility.

goal.description: The packet's goal in the plan's own words, so a judge compares the return against what was asked and not against what was done.

inputs.description: Every file the packet was given, each pinned by content so a judge reads the same bytes the builder read.

path.description: Absolute or repository-relative path of the input.

sha256.description: sha256 of the input's bytes as read, bare hex or sha256:-prefixed.

repository.description: Id of the configured source repository that owns path (repository {action: list}); path is then that repository's coordinate, as repository.read returned it. Absent: path is a project artifact, manuscript source, a repository-relative workspace path or absolute.

source.description: Use a real Git checkpoint or exact source/artifact handles. A declared contract requiring a commit still requires the Git alternative for COMPLETE; non-Git manuscript/research work does not invent Git IDs.

branch.description: The lane branch the work is committed on; never master and never pushed.

base_commit.description: The commit the lane branched from.

candidate.description: Exact Git checkpoint identity, or null only for noncomplete work with pinned continuation artifacts. Never fabricate a commit.

candidate_parent.description: Exact Git checkpoint identity, or null only for noncomplete work with pinned continuation artifacts. Never fabricate a commit.

candidate_tree.description: Exact Git checkpoint identity, or null only for noncomplete work with pinned continuation artifacts. Never fabricate a commit.

worktree.description: Absolute path of the worktree left in place for the judge, or the word removed with where the branch lives.

kind.description: Source carried by exact artifact pins, including downloaded workspaces without Git.

root.description: The declared source/workspace root for retained paths; a location, not independent write authority.

artifacts.description: Existing source and artifact bytes that establish the result; use the same path/sha256 vocabulary as input pins.

output.description: Exact report/output artifact bytes. COMPLETE requires a readable current path and matching digest; null is allowed only when noncomplete work has not produced an output.

files_written.description: Every path this packet created or changed, repository-relative; the judge's diff must contain no more than these.

summary.description: What was established, in plain technical English; the only field the harness envelope repeats.

most_important.description: The findings a reader must not miss, ordered; each one a claim, not a topic.

scripted_check.description: A real command check or receipt-bound declared-owner read. Existing executable command obligations cannot be satisfied by a generic read.

profile.description: Optional: a measurement of the organ this packet built, when the packet's brief names a profile entry (distil.py profile).

verdict.description: Inherent work or overhead, in the profiler's own words.

overhead_share.description: Fraction of wall time that was overhead rather than the work itself.

residuals.description: DEMONSTRATED impossibilities only, never a list of what was skipped: empty when status is COMPLETE and non-empty exactly when it is DEMONSTRATED-IMPOSSIBILITY.

clause.description: The sentence of the brief or the line of the tree that the demonstration contradicts.

failing_command.description: The command whose observed output is the demonstration, with its result.

smallest_change.description: The smallest change that would close it, and whose decision it is.

remaining_work.description: Concrete recoverable work, separate from proven impossibility. Noncomplete standing requires at least one item; COMPLETE and demonstrated impossibility carry no fixable remainder here.

work.description: The unmet part of the declared task.

reason.description: Observed reason it remains: implementation gap, missing dependency, quota interruption or other concrete evidence.

next_action.description: A concrete next action for the successor to assess against retained current bytes.

continuation.description: A reconstruction handoff for INCOMPLETE/BLOCKED/INTERRUPTED; null for terminal completion or demonstrated impossibility. No time/turn cutoff or replay instruction is implied.

artifacts.description: Exact retained source, input, patch, output or execution evidence handles for reconstruction; preserved effects are inspected before any continuation.

next_action.description: The first explicit continuation action; no automatic rerun is authorized.

resume_condition.description: What must be observed before proceeding, such as quota restored, dependency supplied, or retained changes reconciled.

path.description: An existing source, output, patch or evidence path whose bytes are retained; absolute or relative to the declared root.

sha256.description: Exact current retained bytes; never an invented hash or a claim that resumed work replays safely.

repository.description: Id of the configured source repository that owns path (repository {action: list}); path is then that repository's coordinate, as repository.read returned it. Absent: path is a project artifact, manuscript source, a repository-relative workspace path or absolute.

command.description: The declared exact check command, even when interruption prevented its execution.

exit_code.description: Observed exit status, or null when no exit status was observed. COMPLETE requires PASSED and zero.

output_tail.description: The check's final output, verbatim, enough of it to read the verdict.

state.description: Whether this exact check passed, failed, was interrupted, or was not run.

kind.description: An actually executed or declared command check.
A declared-owner read; no OS command exit is fabricated.

state.description: Observed execution state of the declared read check.

operation.description: The canonical read operation actually invoked, or declared when NOT_RUN.

payload.description: Exact canonical request payload from the existing read receipt.

receipt_id.description: Existing READ receipt ID from the actual worker/reviewer turn, null when no successful read receipt exists.

output_sha256.description: Existing receipt digest of consulted owner result before attaching receipt metadata.

ok.description: Observed read success, null if not run; validated against the actual receipt/context.

output_tail.description: Observed result or exact reason this read check did not run.
